note: Pager Serializer provides a Views REST-export style plugin (id pager_serializer, extends core rest Serializer) that outputs serialized rows plus a pager object (current_page, total_items, total_pages, items_per_page). Requires core rest. All labels/flags come from config object pager_serializer.settings (form route pager_serializer.settings at /admin/config/pager_serializer; reset route pager_serializer.settings.reset), which ships config/install defaults (rows/pager, all *_enabled true, standard *_label names). Each row can be altered via hook_pager_serializer_row_alter. Core permission administer site configuration; no own permission/Drush/new plugin type. Medium/hard scripts set and read these real config keys and restore the shipped defaults.

evals.prompt: What does the pager_serializer module add to a Drupal Views REST export response compared with the standard Serializer?
evals.expected_output: It wraps the serialized rows (under a 'rows' key) alongside a 'pager' object containing current_page, total_items, total_pages and items_per_page, which the standard Serializer omits.

evals.prompt: How do I actually use pager_serializer on a Views REST export display so my API returns pagination data?
evals.expected_output: On the View's REST export display, set the Format/style to 'Pager serializer' (the pager_serializer Views style) instead of the default Serializer, add a pager, and choose the accepted formats. Requires the core rest module.

evals.prompt: Which hook does pager_serializer provide to add or change a field on each serialized row of a REST export?
evals.expected_output: hook_pager_serializer_row_alter(&$row, \Drupal\views\ResultRow $result, \Drupal\views\ViewExecutable $view) — mutate $row (passed by reference), typically gated on $view->id().

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the pager_serializer configuration: what property name will the total number of items be returned under in the API output, and is the current-page field currently included?
evals.expected_output: total_items_label is 'count' (so totals appear under 'count'), and current_page_enabled is false so the current page field is not included.

evals.prompt: On this site, will pager_serializer nest the pagination fields inside their own object, or merge them onto the top-level response? Inspect the live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: pager_object_enabled is false, so the pager fields are flattened onto the top-level response object rather than nested under a 'pager' key.

evals.prompt: Configure pager_serializer on this site so the pagination object is returned under the property name 'meta' and the current page is returned under 'page'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set pager_serializer.settings: pager_label='meta' and current_page_label='page' (e.g. drush cset pager_serializer.settings pager_label meta; drush cset pager_serializer.settings current_page_label page).

evals.prompt: Configure pager_serializer on this site so the REST export output no longer includes the total number of pages, and so the items-per-page value is returned under the property name 'per_page'. Apply the change to the live site.
